99. **`b39_star.py`'s illumination criterion cannot report the Moon absent — it counts the whole frame, which the star field dominates.** [measured 2026-08-26 off the instrument's own committed artifacts, §11.149(d6); instrument defect, the §11.101(g)/§11.53(d) criterion-that-cannot-discriminate class] `harness/b39_star.py:67-68` defines `lit(tag)` as *every pixel of the 2048² frame whose max channel exceeds 16*, and the scene it judges runs `flag landscape off` + `flag atmosphere off` with the Moon at fov 30 — so the count is dominated by the star field and the milky-way glow: **15 462 px of background against ~1 850 px of Moon**. When `body name Sun hidden true` parks the whole Sun subtree and the Moon leaves the frame entirely, the number moves 17 302 → 15 462, an 11 % change that the entry read as *"the Moon stays lit"*. There is no body-local region of interest, no off-body background control, and **no state in which the criterion could report the subject absent**; the sibling `dpx()` metric was attributed to the Sun (*"the Sun's own disc and halo leaving the frame"*) when the Sun's own dump record reads `visible: false` in BOTH frames and 95.0 % of the differing pixels lie within 150 px of the Moon's centre. The fix must also re-point the entry's claim, never loosen it. The tree holds exactly TWO `Translator` objects — `Translator::globalTranslator`, the one behind `_()` and reassigned by `App::setAppLanguage` `[observed: translator.cpp:43, :44-45; app.cpp:937]`, and `Core::skyTranslator`, reassigned by `Core::setSkyLanguage` `[observed: core.cpp:85, :1585]` — and those four are EVERY construction in the tree `[measured: grep `Translator(` over src/]`. Consequence: `set sky_locale <x>`, `set app_locale <x>` and the TUI locale item `[observed: uiModule/ui_tuiconf.cpp:882]` each refill the ONE table from THAT locale's file, after which the other consumer falls back to English for every key the new file lacks — silently, since a miss returns the input. The default install hides it: `app_locale` and `sky_locale` are both `fr` in the shipped config and both translators read `<languageDir><locale>.txt` `[observed: ~/.spacecrafter/config.ini:68,71 — host-local, untracked]`. THREE riders on the same object: **(a)** the header promises *"If the passed locale name cannot be handled by the system, default value will be used"* `[observed: translator.hpp:46-47]` and no such fallback exists — `langName` is stored verbatim `[:49-50]`, which is also the fact that made §5.119's `zh` branch unconditional; **(b)** a missing locale file produces NO diagnostic — `reload()` clears the table, fails to open, returns silently `[:84-112]`, so an unknown locale is accepted, reported as success, and empties the translations (§2(f) unmet; same silent-acceptance class as §5.116 and §5.118, different mechanism: a resource that did not load, not a value that was coerced); **(c)** `lastUsed` is an identity test against a raw pointer that DANGLES after every reassignment — `skyTranslator = Translator(...)` fills the table from a temporary and then destroys it `[observed: core.cpp:1585, app.cpp:937 against translator.cpp:52-53]` — so a later temporary at the same stack address would make `reload()` return early and never load the new locale [derived: address reuse at a fixed call site is plausible, NOT measured]. DISTINCT from **§5.28**, which is the same file and the same author's habits but another defect (`getAvailableLanguagesCodes`'s `pop_back` on an empty join, fixed at source 2026-08-04): this row is about who owns the table. — **OPEN** (found 2026-09-01 by F74 en route, minted under §5.79's reachable-with-consequence criterion; **record-don't-fix**: which locale should own a shared table is a product question, and rider (c)'s repair is a lifetime redesign of a static — both Vixy's, and both compose with D9 since a field show may already depend on whichever locale currently wins. **Owed before it is judged**: unmeasured — one launch driving `set sky_locale zh_CN` on a `fr` UI would show whether the UI strings revert to English, and a second `set sky_locale` in the same run would settle rider (c) by showing whether the new file is loaded at all.)

122. **An argument KEY the handler never reads is unobservable to everyone: `args` is a `std::map` read with `operator[]`, so "the author did not write this key" and "the author wrote it with an empty value" are ONE state, and a key the author DID write that no handler reads costs a silence — 39 lines of the shipped script package are in exactly that state today.** [observed 2026-09-01 by F76 (scedit journal `2026-09-01b`) while dispositioning the 1661 findings over the 408 installed scripts; READ at `e3afca8f` and CONFIRMED LIVE on a fresh launch] `parseCommand` writes every `key value` pair of a line into `arguments[key]` whatever the key is `[observed: app_command_interface.cpp:164-182]` — there is no vocabulary check at parse time and none anywhere after it. Each handler then reads the keys it knows with `std::string arg = args[W_X];` and branches on `.empty()` (e.g. `commandDeselect` `[observed: :3314-3322]`, `commandAudio` `[:3037-3095]`, `commandDate` `[:3964-4108]`, `commandDso` `[:1599-1620]`). Two consequences follow from `operator[]` on a `std::map<std::string,std::string>` `[observed: src/tools/utility.hpp:85]`, and they are the whole row: **(a)** a key nobody reads is never looked at, so the command runs its normal path and `executeCommandStatus` reports SUCCESS with `debug_message` untouched `[observed: :1307-1341]`; **(b)** a key a handler DOES read but the author never wrote default-constructs to `""`, which is the same value an explicitly empty key would give — so the handler cannot distinguish absent from empty even if it wanted to. **Measured on the field corpus, not derived**: 39 lines across 8 shipped scripts carry a key no handler reads — `deselect … pointer` ×27, `audio … output_rate` ×9, `media … key_color` ×2 (the engine's spelling is `keycolor` `[observed: base_command_interface.hpp:189]`), `date … duration` ×1 — and 5 more lines (`internal/deepsky_drawings.sts`) reach the same state by ACCIDENT, an unquoted two-word `credit` shifting the pairing so that `texture_luminance_adjust` never becomes a key and `evalDouble("")` hands `loadNebula` 0.0 instead of the 1 the line asks for `[observed: :1613-1616, :4631-4635]`. Confirmed live on a fresh launch: `deselect constellation Dor pointer off` was echoed as executed and produced no diagnostic of any kind `[measured: harness/f76_live.py leg E]`. DISTINCT from §5.116 (which is the VALUE half — a chokepoint coercing an unrecognised value to OFF or 0; this is the KEY half, and it has no chokepoint at all, which is the mechanism), from §5.118 (a post-parse semantic guard swallowing a parsed value) and from §5.117 (severity: these records do not exist to have a severity). COMPOSES with both: where §5.116 makes a wrong value silent and §5.117 makes a refusal look like trace, this makes a wrong NAME leave no record whatever — so a script's author has no channel through which a misspelt key could ever reach them. §11.177(d)'s belief-lag argument applies at full strength: 39 shipped lines have been carrying words their authors believe are doing something. — **OPEN** (found and minted 2026-09-01 by F76 under the §5.79 criterion — reachable with consequence from a shipped surface, and here reached by shipped content; **record-don't-fix**: the repair is a product decision and a large one — a vocabulary check at parse time would refuse lines that run today, so it cuts straight across §2.0 D9, and the alternative reading is that a permissive parser is deliberate and the missing piece is a `--check` tool, which now exists. Vixy's fork, and it composes with §5.116's class decision: refusing an unknown VALUE while ignoring an unknown NAME would be an odd place to stop. **Owed before it is judged**: nothing on the mechanism — both halves are at source and the field instances are measured; what is owed is the owner's reading of whether the permissiveness was a choice.) **[EXTENDED 2026-09-04, F80 §11.200(b) → §5.124: the same mechanism runs on the DATA surface and is two orders of magnitude larger there — 189 lines of the field `ssystem.ini` and 164 of `data/default_ssystem.ini` carry keys no loader reads, plus 3365 shipped SCRIPT lines carrying three misspellings that this row's own class makes unobservable. This row's *"39 lines of the shipped script package"* was the unknown-parameter subset scedit could SEE at the time; `body`'s key vocabulary was not checkable until the stellar-system contract existed, which is why the real figure was out of reach rather than wrong.]**

123. **The engine's "did you mean" for a `set` line names the wrong argument: it suggests a neighbour for `args.begin()->first` — the alphabetically FIRST key on the line — and not for the key that actually failed, so on any multi-key `set` the advice points at an innocent name, sometimes one that was applied successfully.** [observed 2026-09-01 by F76 while verifying a corpus finding LIVE; the source read at `e3afca8f`, the behaviour then reproduced on a running engine] `evalCommandSet` reaches `case SCD_NAMES::APP_FLAG_NONE` with the failing name in its own parameter `setName`, and calls `appInit->searchSimilarSet(args.begin()->first)` `[observed: app_command_interface.cpp:2384-2391]` — the map's first key by sort order, which is the failing one only when the failure happens to sort first. **Measured, both ways, on one launch** `[measured: harness/f76_live.py leg F]`: `set zzz_f76bogus 1 heading 99` logged *"heading is unknown. Did you mean heading ?"*, correct by the accident of sort order. The shipped instance is of the second kind: `fscripts/S13.sts:2` `set home_planet Earth duration 0` says *"duration is unknown. Did you mean heading ?"* — the right subject, and a suggestion pointing away from `home_planet` (SS-35, and the same shape as SS-22's `mod` → "did you mean mode?"). Composes with the SHORT-CIRCUIT at the same site: `commandSet` folds `returnValue = returnValue && evalCommandSet(...)` over the map `[observed: :2273-2287]`, so the first failing key in sort order stops the line — the two together mean a multi-key `set` can lose a real setting AND be told the wrong thing about why. DISTINCT from §5.117 (severity: this record reaches the log at the right place, it is the CONTENT that is wrong) and from §5.116 (values). §2(f)'s "actionable" fails here on a channel that was built to be actionable — a suggester that names a key which worked is worse than none. — **OPEN** (found and minted 2026-09-01 by F76; **record-don't-fix**: the repair looks like one identifier — `setName` in place of `args.begin()->first` — but the shipped diagnostic TEXT changes for every multi-key `set` in the field, which is user-visible output on §5.115's uncapped log, and the sibling emitters must be checked for the same shape before the class is called one line: `searchSimilarFlag(name)` `[observed: :456]` and `searchSimilarCommand(command)` `[:379]` both pass the failing token and look correct, which is what makes this one an outlier rather than a pattern — but that is an argument from two samples. **Owed before it is judged**: a census of every `searchSimilar*` call site with the value it passes, which F58's instrument shape would answer cheaply.)

source ABSENT → `ec` **true**, message `"No such file or directory"` → *"Completed copy"*, the same arm, destination left at **0 entries**. **Reach, and it is not hypothetical**: this repository installs NO content (§11.204(f) — no `textures`, `stars`, `sky_cultures`, `landscapes`, `fonts`, `audio`, `scripts`, `model3D`, `language`, `videos`), so on any machine where only the tree was installed the first launch prints **ten** *"Completed copy of …"* lines and creates ten empty directories with no error on any channel; 133. **The anchor loader keeps a pointer to an orbit that has already been destroyed — `.get()` on a temporary `unique_ptr` — and every `type = orbit` section of the shipped `anchor.ini` builds one.** [§5.127(2)'s member, promoted to its own row 2026-09-05 by F86 and re-verified at the code at `1cbd6780`; found 2026-09-04 by F80, §11.200(e)(2)] `AnchorPointOrbitCreator::handle` does `Orbit * orbit = orbitCreator->handle(params).get();` `[observed: navModule/anchor_creator_cor.cpp:130]`. Every creator in the chain returns `std::unique_ptr<Orbit>` `[observed: bodyModule/orbit_creator_cor.hpp:34]`, so the returned temporary is destroyed at the end of that full expression and `orbit` dangles from the next statement on; it is then stored into an `AnchorPointOrbit` at `:147` (no parent) and `:156` (with parent). **Nothing ever owned it after the creator returned**: the member is a raw `Orbit *` `[observed: navModule/anchor_point_orbit.hpp:57]` and the destructor's only statement is a commented-out `//delete orbit;` `[observed: anchor_point_orbit.cpp:37]` — the class was written for a raw `new` that the chain stopped doing. **Reach, on the shipped file**: `~/.spacecrafter/anchor.ini` declares THREE `type = orbit` anchors — `orbit_autour_lune` (`ell_orbit`), `orbit_autour_point` (`phobos_special`), `baryEarthMoon` (`barycenter`, `:53-61`) — and `AnchorManager::load` constructs every section at startup `[observed: navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:226-258, :271-280]`. The dangling pointer is DEREFERENCED by `AnchorPointOrbit::update` `[observed: anchor_point_orbit.cpp:44]`, which runs when such an anchor is the current one — one shipped command away: `camera action switch name orbit_autour_lune` `[observed: interfaceModule/app_command_interface.cpp:4597-4602 → bodyModule/ssystem_factory.hpp:896 → anchor_manager.cpp:357]`. **Why no launch had ever caught it**: `init_location:home_planet` makes the startup anchor an `AnchorPointBody`, and `AnchorManager::update` calls `update()` on the current anchor only `[observed: anchor_manager.cpp:303-306]` (or, in eye-relative mode, only where `isOnBody()` `[:293]`), so the pointer is stored on every launch and read on none of them — which is also why a plain ASan startup is silent. — **FIXED 2026-09-05 by F86, code `a4a7c226`** (row minted OPEN first, per the session-21 granularity ruling *"§5.127 is a bundle; any member scheduled gets its own row first"*). **REPRODUCED UNDER ASan BEFORE BEING TOUCHED** [measured, §11.205(c); reports `harness/artifacts/f86/asan_pre_switch.report.txt`, `asan_pre_quarantine.report.txt`]: one shipped command, `camera action switch name orbit_autour_lune`, and ASan aborts on a **READ of size 8** at `orbit.hpp:36` (the vptr load of the virtual `positionAtTimevInVSOP87Coordinates`) ← `AnchorPointOrbit::update` `anchor_point_orbit.cpp:44` ← `AnchorManager::update:306` — the predicted stack exactly. **The prediction's CLASS was refuted and is kept**: ASan reports `heap-buffer-overflow`, never names the free, and `quarantine_size_mb=1024` does not change it — by the time the anchor is read the orbit's memory has been recycled and its chunk identity is gone, so this is a virtual call through a vptr in re-used heap, which is worse than "reads stale but intact bytes". **The RELEASE binary takes the same command without crashing** (exit 0, predicted): the corruption is silent on the shipped build. **FIX, at the ownership (I5), not at the symptom**: `AnchorPointOrbit` now takes and holds a `std::unique_ptr<Orbit>` — the anchor is the only user and outlives every use — the creator `std::move`s it in at both call sites, and the destructor is defaulted in the `.cpp` (the header only forward-declares `Orbit`); the commented-out `//delete orbit;` is gone with the raw pointer it belonged to. **PROVED**: the identical ASan launch is **clean, exit 0**; `b4_anchors` green on every geometric check; the full canary **12/12 in band, every delta 0.0**, dwell frame md5 unchanged. **[WHAT THE PRE-FIX BINARY WAS DRAWING — measured 2026-09-05 by F89, §11.208(f)(h), on the RELEASE builds: this defect was never silent, only non-fatal. One `camera action switch` onto any `type = orbit` anchor and the OLD path's observer sits **237 022 km** from where the anchor says it is — its own dump reads `Moon.old.dist` **182 582.8 km** against `b4_orbit_moon`'s authored **200 000.0 km**, identical to the tenth of a kilometre in seven runs across two sessions and two build directories, while every NEW-path field (`camera.mat`, `camera.rootPos`, the anchor body's `ecl`) is byte-identical to the fixed binary's. One tracking command later the old path aims **76.46°** from the body it was told to follow (0.35° on the fixed binary, 0.000° once settled), and since the star field is drawn by the OLD pipeline (`executorModule/solarSystemModule.cpp:298`) the shipped build composed its sky for a different piece of the celestial sphere than the bodies in front of it: `nbStarsToDraw` 3446 vs 3573, ~22 000 px of star field elsewhere, the Moon's centroid unmoved. This also names the cause of the ONE red §11.205(g) left open, and a third binary carrying §5.134's guard ALONE reproduces the pre-fix numbers exactly, so the attribution to THIS fix is measured and not inferred. The row stays FIXED; what changes is the severity it records.]** **[THE GATE THAT CATCHES THIS CLASS EXISTS SINCE 2026-09-05, F93 §11.210: `b4_anchors`' P1b asserts the OLD path's distance to an orbit anchor's parent against the AUTHORED semi-major axis at 13 dumps of its scene, tolerance 1.0 km against 17417 km of discrimination — the pre-fix binary reds 9 times, the fixed one greens 13/13, twice. A regression of this row now fails a landed gate instead of passing one. It also refines the OBSERVABILITY: an anchor created by `camera action create` seconds before it is read reports its authored radius correctly on the pre-fix binary, while the one loaded from `anchor.ini` at startup is 17417 km out — same dangling pointer, different allocator luck, which is §11.205(c)'s ASan finding from the other end.]** | **§11.205(c)(d)**, **§11.208(f)(h)**, **§11.210**, §5.127(2), §11.200(e), R4

134. **A comet orbit whose parent name does not resolve crashes the loader on the one branch that needs a parent — the same function established, sixty lines earlier, that the parent may be null.** [§5.127(1)'s member, promoted to its own row 2026-09-05 by F86 and re-verified at the code at `1cbd6780`; found 2026-09-04 by F80, §11.200(e)(1)] `OrbitCreatorComet::handle` looks the parent up by name `[observed: bodyModule/orbit_creator_cor.cpp:118]` and treats a null result as a SUPPORTED case: `if(!parent)` reads `parent_rot_obliquity` / `parent_rot_asc_node` / `parent_rot_J2000_longitude` from the section instead `[:124-128]`. Sixty lines later, on the branch taken when BOTH `orbit_meanmotion` and `orbit_period` are absent, it calls `parent->get_parent()` unconditionally `[:183]`. **The shipped data runs that branch on every launch**: of the six `coord_func = comet_orbit` sections in `~/.spacecrafter/ssystem.ini`, **five** (Pallas, Juno, Vesta, Haumea, Makemake) carry neither key and reach `:183` `[measured 2026-09-05, F86: 91 sections, 6 comet, 5 without either key; `data/default_ssystem.ini` 79/6/**6**]` — they survive only because `parent = Sun` resolves. **Two channels reach it with a null parent.** (1) `anchor.ini` and the `camera action create` command: `AnchorPointOrbitCreator::handle` builds the orbit BEFORE it looks at the parent `[observed: anchor_creator_cor.cpp:130 vs :137/:153]`, so an anchor section with `coord_func = comet_orbit`, no period and a parent name that does not resolve reaches `:183` with `parent == nullptr` and no check in between. (2) `ssystem.ini` with `parent = none`, which `ProtoSystem::addBody` keeps as a null parent and adds anyway `[observed: bodyModule/protosystem.cpp:528-537]`; a *misspelled* parent, by contrast, is stopped at `:533`. The experimental reader already carries the guard as an `isNotSystemCentered` flag `[observed: experimentalModule/orbitModules/CometOrbitLoader.hpp:4, :13-14, :61-64]`, so the two paths disagree on the same authored file: one logs and drops the body, the other dies. — **FIXED 2026-09-05 by F86, code `a4a7c226`** (row minted OPEN first, same ruling as §5.133). **The guard is the experimental reader's semantics ported**, §11.205(e): the question `:183` means to ask is *"is this orbit centred on the system centre"*, so it is asked as a flag set where the answer is known — a parent that was not found is NOT the system centre, because nothing there can know that it is. The existing message is kept **verbatim** for the case that already reached the line (as-if on that channel); the case that used to segfault gets a **§2(f) diagnostic naming the section, the parent it looked for and the two keys that fix it**. **MEASURED THREE WAYS** on a scratch section in the FARM's `ssystem.ini` only [artifacts `harness/artifacts/f86/section_nokeys.ini`, `result_comet_*.json.gz`]: pre-fix **SIGSEGV** (returncode −11), TCP never opened, during the load; post-fix **exit 0** with the diagnostic, `protosystem.cpp`'s *"Error when creating orbit from …"* and the body absent; **control** — the same section plus `orbit_period` — loads on the PRE-fix binary, so the crash is the missing pair and not the section. **Unplanned finding**: the same pre-fix applog shows the NEW path already logging its own version of this and skipping the body **1448 log-ticks before** the old path died on it — one authored file, two readers, one of which crashed. The class was checked, not assumed: `OrbitCreatorEliptic` never dereferences a null parent and `OrbitCreatorBary` tests both bodies, so it is confined to this one line. **[ANNOTATED 2026-09-05 by F89, §11.208(g) — this guard was TESTED IN ISOLATION AND EXONERATED: it was BUILT ALONE and run, to attribute the `b4_anchors` P7 red between the two fixes that shipped in `a4a7c226`. A binary carrying this guard with §5.133's ownership fix reverted reproduces the PRE-fix numbers on every observable — control PASS 45 < 217, `Moon.old.dist` 182 582.8 km, 76.46°, `nbStarsToDraw` 3446, and 0–2 px of lit-set difference from the pre-fix binary — so nothing in this row is implicated in that red, and the attribution to §5.133 is measured rather than argued. Nothing about this row's own state changes.]** | **§11.205(e)**, **§11.208(g)**, §5.127(1), §11.200(e), §2(f), R4
135. **The OLD path turns the view offset WITH the heading, so changing the heading shifts where the offset puts the image on the dome — the tester has seen it and says it should not happen.** [mechanism observed 2026-09-05 at code `a2fd3c5b`; behaviour tester-confirmed, round-3 R28] `Navigator::updateViewMat` pitches the eye by the offset — `mat_local_to_eye = Mat4d::xrotation(view_offset * fov/2 * M_PI/180 * view_offset_transition) * mat_local_to_eye` `[observed: navModule/navigator.cpp:324]` — and then LEFT-MULTIPLIES the heading roll onto that result, `Mat4d::zrotation(heading*M_PI/180 + 0.0001) * mat_local_to_eye` `[observed: :329]`. Left-multiplication puts the roll in the OUTER (eye) frame, so it rotates the already-offset frame and the offset's direction on the dome turns with the heading. The NEW path applies the offset in the physical eye frame (screen/dome-fixed), which is why the two match exactly at heading 0 and only there — old's chain slot was tried on the new path and corrupted B13's held-reference composition by a measured **2.06° absDelta** (§11.92(d), the conscious deviation this row now vindicates). **The tester's statement is the requirement**: *"The offset is screen dependant. The change of heading shouldn't shift the offset position. I saw that it does now but it shouldn't"* `[stated: tester (Lionel RUIZ), via owner commit 6ffb017]` — screen-dependent, must not move with heading, and he has OBSERVED the movement. **Why this is a defect and not a divergence**: §11.52(b) makes old the baseline *conditioned on old being physically exact*, and the field authority for this surface has now stated the opposite intent with an observation behind it, so the old behaviour has no requirement left to protect. **Reach**: OLD path only, from shipped surfaces — `set heading` / `heading delta_azimuth` composed with config `[navigation] view_offset` or `set zoom_offset`; §5.79's criterion met, tester-confirmed. **Sibling, not duplicate**: §5.128 is the *other* old-path offset defect (the aim site compensating a FIXED `× 90°` at `:162` while the draw applies `× fov/2` at `:324`); this row is the heading coupling, and the two are independent. Citation drift closed while minting: B17's row cites `:159`/`:309` for these sites, which are the pre-drift coordinates; at `a2fd3c5b` they are `:162` and `:324`. — **OPEN, and the fix is NOT decision-free.** Its DIRECTION is settled (dome-fixed wins, R28), but the change lands on the comparison baseline, which is unchanged by construction (§11.52(b)): whether the old path may be corrected at all, or must carry the defect until it retires with B8, is the owner's call — **both readings recorded, neither taken.** | **§11.207(e)**, §11.92(d), §11.198(d), B17, §5.128, §5.66, §5.71, R28

136. **`app_locale` does nothing whenever it differs from `sky_locale`: the two settings share ONE catalogue map, the last one loaded wins, and the app logs the locale it is about to discard.** [measured 2026-09-05, §11.209(f) (F87); four farm launches, byte-exact 2×2] `Translator` declares BOTH its state members `static` — `static Translator* lastUsed;` and `static std::map<std::string, std::string> m_translator;` `[observed: tools/translator.hpp:83-85]` — so every `Translator` instance in the process shares one map, and `translateUTF8` reads it `[translator.cpp:156-163]`. `App::setAppLanguage` assigns a fresh `Translator` to `globalTranslator` `[app.cpp:937]` and `Core::setSkyLanguage` assigns one to `skyTranslator` `[core.cpp:1585]`; each constructor calls `reload()`, which **clears the shared map and refills it from its own `<lang>.txt`** `[translator.cpp:80-119]`. Startup runs `setAppLanguage` from config `[app.cpp:625-628]` and `setSkyLanguage` after it `[core.cpp:510-512]` — applog, one run: `Application locale is en` at `010544`, `Sky locale is fr` at `010545` — so `_()`, which reads `globalTranslator`, answers in the **sky** locale. **Measured, 90 bodies × 4 printed strings, sidecars byte-compared**: `(app=fr, sky=fr)` and `(app=en, sky=fr)` are IDENTICAL (md5 `7e14412d`, French); `(app=en, sky=en)` and `(app=fr, sky=en)` are IDENTICAL (md5 `4e56907c`, English). **`app_locale` has zero effect on what the user reads, and a FRENCH app locale produces an ENGLISH interface when the sky locale is English.** **Reach, three shipped surfaces**: `config.ini`'s `[localization] app_locale` `[define_key.hpp:127]`; the TUI's own locale menu `[ui_tuiconf.cpp:882]`; and TCP/script `set ui_locale` `[app_command_interface.cpp:2351]` — each accepted, echoed to the log, and then silently overridden, which is also a §2.0 D12 miss (an acting override, unlogged, contradicting the value the app just reported). Scope note: because the two shipped locales are normally set alike, the FIELD is unaffected today — the defect is latent until someone sets them apart, which the TUI invites. **Second hazard on the same lines, recorded UNMEASURED**: `reload()`'s early return `if (Translator::lastUsed == this) return;` compares against a pointer that is routinely a **destroyed temporary** (the `Translator(dir, lang)` built for the assignment), so a later allocation landing on that address would skip a reload entirely. — **OPEN** (found 2026-09-05 by F87 when its ENGLISH CONTROL printed French; record-don't-fix, out of that task's scope. The repair is a design choice, not a patch: one map per instance, or one translator with two named domains, or an explicit reload order — and the third only hides it. Owed before it is judged: whether the sky translator's map and the UI's should ever have been one, which is a question for whoever owns `sky_locale`'s meaning.) | §11.209(f), §5.111, §2.0 D12

## 8. Threading / handoff strategy — PROPOSAL v2 (2026-07-11, pending Vixy convergence)

Successor to the strategy.txt task-at-draw sketch (confirmed best-found-at-the-time [vixy: 2026-07-11]). v1 proposed a single global completion queue; the EntityCore/Executor inventory (§8.6) found that Vixy's in-progress `Taskable` primitive [observed: EntityCore/Executor/Taskable.hpp, written 2026-07-11] provides strict per-body ordering [vixy: 2026-07-11 — named requirement] and a *better* resolution of the MPSC transient-window than v1's defer-retry. v2 is the synthesis. Once converged and implemented, the authoritative home of each contract becomes the header of the component owning it; this section then reduces to a pointer.

### 8.1 Constraints it must satisfy
C1 no loading↔drawing race · C2 no body destruction with pending tasks · C3 draw thread never blocks · C4 loader threads may block · strict per-body task ordering · burst absorption without idle-case cost (D7) · shared-resource dedup + fan-out (D7) · minimal overhead · D5 hardware ranges · D6 texture/model asymmetry (all [vixy: 2026-07-11]).

### 8.2 Shape: per-body Taskable chains + global ready-list, boundary-localized lock-freedom
Lock-free machinery exists **only** where the render thread meets producers; loader-side internals may block (C4 — INT-2: complexity lives where the binding boundary is).

1. **The render chain is an "effective thread"** [vixy: 2026-07-11]: draw-visible state is protected by one render-side `Taskable`; everything touching that state runs as a Task on its chain. Sequential consistency comes from the Taskable ordering promise, **not from thread identity** — rendering itself may occasionally execute on a worker or events thread, and that is correct by design. C1 = chain serialization; per-body publish ordering is automatic (a single FIFO chain preserves per-key order). The chain **may and should go idle** — see the stack note in 4.
2. **Main loop** [vixy: 2026-07-11, corrected 2nd pass]: a pure cadencer at the target framerate — `execute()`s the **frame task** onto the render chain (inplace when idle, lowest latency; chained behind pending publishes otherwise) and waits until the next tick. **Update+draw live inside the frame task itself** — one Task, scheduled/executed every frame [vixy]: the residual synchronous update part is cheap, cache-local, and uses the exact elapsed time in non-recording mode.
3. **Two protection domains** `[inferred — effectively confirmed by the fence discipline below]`: work tasks/chains do the hard work and the async sequencing (completion events: the chain waits, no thread waits) and **never touch draw-visible state**; their final step schedules a lightweight subscribe/finalize/publish task onto the render chain [vixy: 2026-07-11 — "tasks on the Taskable for rendering only subscribe/finalize the render-thread-side part, not doing hard work"]. **Fence discipline** [vixy: 2026-07-11, 2nd pass]: fence waits happen as late as possible, only where the touched resource requires them, and **only the rendering part ever waits on a fence** — with multiple frames in flight, the acquire/present semaphore structure makes an actual block genuinely unlikely; the fence is the guarantee, not the expected wait. The separation restated with this: long holds belong to the work domain; the render chain carries only late, rarely-blocking guarantees. Starvation-free: publish execution is independent of whether the body is drawn (closes the D3 channel of the at-draw sketch).
4. **Cost profile**: idle = zero — no drain point exists; the render chain sleeps between frame tasks. Per completion = the work chain's exchanges + one publish push. Bursts chain behind the frame task and execute between frames as O(N) lightweight publishes (heavy work — decode, build, upload — already done in the work domain; a publish is a pointer/descriptor swap, O(small) by contract). **Stack note** [vixy: 2026-07-11]: synchronous `endTask` cascades nest on the stack (unless tail-call optimization applies), so chains going idle is *preferable* — it resets the depth; bounded bursts (D7) are the sizing assumption.
5. **Lifetime (C2) under the granularity decision** [vixy: 2026-07-11, 2nd pass]: synchronization goes through a **single Taskable** — the render chain — likely sufficient granularity, and cheaply revisable if it turns out wrong, thanks to how Task/Taskable compose [vixy]. **All Taskables live for the whole application duration** → `TASKABLE_REFERENCE_COUNT`/`TASKABLE_TASK_KEEP_REFERENCE` stay off. Two consequences:
   - **Pins need no atomics at all**: pin increments (request emission, inside the frame task) and decrements (publish/finalization tasks) both execute within the effective thread — a plain integer under chain serialization.
   - **The hand-off rule stops being discipline and becomes forced**: with a non-atomic pin, worker code *cannot* legally release — the only path is transferring the hold into the publish task. The earlier `[inferred]` rule is now enforced by the type, not by convention.
   `remove()` on a pinned body detaches from the tree immediately (world-consistent, ModularBodyPtr::redirect philosophy); memory follows when the pin reaches zero inside the chain. Reopening trigger (membership, not magnitude): sustained publish volume contending with frame-task latency → split to per-body chains — KEEP_REFERENCE returns, and §8.6(f) must be fixed first.
   - Pin counter deliberately **not** merged with render-local `pointerCount` (different synchronization domains; merging forces atomics onto the render-local path — I2: one info, one domain).
   - Module replacement during pending load needs no pin: integration validates `body->slot(id) == module` at drain — render-thread-local, race-free by construction, drops stale payloads.
6. **Requests, priorities, cancellation**: `AsyncBuilder`-style atomic priority field is the existing pattern ("prioritize on activation" = one atomic store); workers re-read at pop and re-check before expensive phases (drops uploads for bodies gone halo-only). Cancelled tasks still schedule a payload-less completion for the unpin. The `LoadPriority` fused state+priority encoding (one atomic carries DONE/COMPLETED/LOADING/LAZY→NOW) is kept — one-word lifecycle — but needs a header comment and the NOW→ACTIVE rename for consistency.
7. **Shared resources (D7)**: the loadable unit is a refcounted resource object (`AsyncBuilder::useCount` pattern exists). Dedup by resource identity at request time (render-side registry; s_texture already dedups by name — verify overlap at plan time). On completion, fan-out = schedule one integration task per attached (body, module) — each push lock-free, per-body order preserved. Attachment-list synchronization: either a small loader-side mutex (legal, C4) or the resource itself as a `Taskable` in `execute` mode (attachments serialized as tasks, no lock) — plan-mode choice.
8. **Texture residency (D6)**: `gc.hpp` is the existing eviction machinery — cycle-based grace (`preservationCycles`) is the hysteresis; `used()` at draw is the relevance mark. Eviction decisions stay render-side; VkImage destruction deferred by frames-in-flight. VRAM budget = D5 parameter with degradation ladder. Models: same pipeline, no eviction path (D6). `gc` cross-thread sync has a known open point (`deletable` non-atomic, flagged in-source) — verify at plan time.
9. **Task semantics — the contract** [vixy: 2026-07-11]: strict ordering applies **only inside `[start(), endTask())`**; a task's `start()` returning does *not* mean the task is done — `endTask` being called on it does; a task must hold nothing with side effects past its `endTask`; outside the window, no guarantee. Tasks/Taskables compose (a Task may hold another Task which calls the enclosing task's `endTask`).
   → **Asynchronous chain holds**: a task may start async work (GPU transfer, fence) and call `endTask` later from wherever completion fires — the *chain* waits, no *thread* waits. This is the natural carrier for the upload→integrate sequence with ordering preserved.
   → ~~Render-hop pattern~~ **SUPERSEDED same day** by the effective-thread model (§8.2.1/3): no thread affinity exists to restore — cross-thread continuation is correct because protection is per-chain, not per-thread; the "hop" is simply the work chain's natural final step of publishing onto the render chain. Kept as a record of the wrong frame (affinity-thinking) it came from.
10. **Thread model** [vixy: 2026-07-11, extended 2nd pass] (concretizes the draft inventory at ModularBody.hpp:131-137): 1 video-player thread (video frame loading) · 1 main thread as cadencer (frame-task `execute` at target framerate, opportunistic inplace execution) · 1 events/scripts thread (SDL event polling, scripts, non-recurrent actions: body building — heavy part lazy — with attachment published as a render-chain Task, orbits/hints display, detach/remove, move, selection) · 1 compute thread (shadow projection, owns a compute VkQueue) [initially forgotten — vixy] · 1 worker executing **only ACTIVE-priority** tasks (a guaranteed free lane for the "needed now" class — reactivity) · nproc−3 generic workers (default, configurable) executing all tasks. The dedicated threads are rarely stressed simultaneously (< 3 active at a time in real-world use) and don't compete with other programs → REALTIME FIFO scheduling shouldn't hurt latency by design [vixy]; the "< 3 active" property is the load-bearing claim, not the exact thread count. **Open integration item** [vixy, initially forgotten]: screen capture for video rendering must fit the task system — `[inferred sketch]` readback rides the render chain after the frame task, encode is worker-domain, file write on the capture path's own ordering.

### 8.3 Rejected alternatives (with rejecting precondition)
- Per-body mutex: C3 + D5-floor (preempted holder stalls render a scheduling quantum); unconditional hot-path cost.
- Task execution at the owning body's draw (strategy.txt sketch): D3 starvation — halo-only bodies never draw → tasks never run → pin/VRAM leak. Its ordering property is retained via Taskable; its execution trigger is replaced by the ready-list drain.
- v1 single global completion queue (2026-07-11, same day): no per-body ordering guarantee across producers (two loaders finishing LoD1/LoD2 of one body can interleave); transient-window handled by defer-retry (one frame latency) where Taskable's marker-exchange resolves it with zero latency and exactly-once continuation. Superseded by §8.2.
- v2.1 never-idle render chain (2026-07-11, same day): a self-rescheduling frame task keeping the chain permanently busy bought "affinity by construction" — at the price of **unbounded stack growth**: synchronous `endTask` cascades nest, and a chain that never ends never resets the depth (unless TCO) [vixy: 2026-07-11]. The stack was the uncounted resource in the "by construction" reasoning. Superseded by the effective-thread model, where idle chains are correct (inplace execution is serialized by the chain promise, no affinity needed) and going idle resets the stack.
- Per-module atomic payload slots: O(visible) per-frame checks for rare events; check cost dominates event cost.
- shared_ptr lifetime: G8. · Generation counters + indirection: same guarantee as pins, more machinery. · Blocking flush on removal: blocks whichever thread removes.

### 8.4 Preconditions (design invalid if violated)
1. **All draw-visible state mutation happens through Tasks on the render chain** — reformulated 2026-07-11 from "on the render thread": the effective-thread model makes physical thread identity irrelevant; what must hold is that no draw-visible state is touched outside the chain. Scripts/events build offline and publish via chain Tasks (e.g. body attachment) — **VERIFIED as the intended management path** [vixy: 2026-07-11].
2. Integration tasks are O(small); violations show as frame spikes at drain (measurable, attributable).
3. Loaders read bodies only via pinned references; mutable inputs are snapshotted into the request at emission (render-side).

### 8.5 Open parameters (plan-mode decisions, not architecture)
Pool sizing policy over 4–64 cores · VRAM budget detection + degradation ladder values · `preservationCycles`/hysteresis values · attachment-list mechanism (mutex vs resource-as-Taskable) · overlap between s_texture dedup and the resource registry · **Task memory-validity flag candidate** (per §8.6.d "maybe worth a new flag"): dual-hold count on Task — init 2 (execution + linkage); `endTask` releases the execution hold (both on CAS-success, since no successor can then exist); the successor's producer releases the linkage hold after its `next.exchange`; at 0 → `recycle()`. Under ifdef, zero overhead when the external guarantee (task embedded in refcounted resource object) is used instead.

### 8.6 EntityCore/Executor inventory (2026-07-11) — reuse map + draft defects
**Reusable as-is or with port**: `AsyncLoaderMgr` (worker pools, BigSave native cache, O_DIRECT once-reads, priority scan, minPriority gate) — its main-thread `update()` pump (O(all-pending) scan per frame, poll not push — I3) is what the ready-list drain replaces; `AsyncBuilder` (refcount + atomic priority + two-phase asyncLoad/postLoad = the resource object pattern); `gc` (eviction/grace); `Taskable`/`Task` (the ordering primitive, in-progress).
**Defects found in the 2026-07-11 `Taskable.hpp` draft** (statuses per Vixy review, 2026-07-11):
- (a) Local shadows member: **RESOLVED on disk** — `execute()` renamed by Vixy; `scheduleExecution()` applied by Claude (2026-07-11, authorized). GCC behavior clarified [vixy]: the new local wins (consistent with the standard point-of-declaration reading; earlier divergence note was a misparse on my side — dissolved).
- (b) Missing memory edge on the marker handoff: **RESOLVED on disk** — producer half (`acq_rel` lines 21/32) by Vixy; consumer half (`endTask` marker exchange → `acq_rel`) applied by Claude (2026-07-11, authorized).
- (c) `Task::start` undefined → link error: **FIXED by Vixy** (now pure virtual; verified on disk 2026-07-11).
- **Contract comments written** (2026-07-11, per Vixy's "specify the promises where they weren't made explicit"): Taskable.hpp carries the full promise block (effective-thread framing, ordering window, completion = endTask, no-affinity, memory validity/marker window, scheduleExecution == false meaning, stack-nesting caution); Task.hpp carries the completion-semantics pointer.
- (d) Node reclamation: **RESOLVED as contract, promises to be written into the headers** [vixy: 2026-07-11 — "definitely worth specifying the promises where they weren't made explicit"]: ordering guarantee only within `[start, endTask)`; task holds nothing with side effects past `endTask`; lifetime via `TASKABLE_TASK_KEEP_REFERENCE` or an external guarantee (ifdef = zero overhead when external); not pooling. Memory residual **confirmed as real and hard to determine externally** [vixy] — a Task's storage must stay valid until successor-linked or chain-empty (the successor's producer may write `task->next` after `endTask` returned); "maybe worth a new flag" [vixy] → candidate design in §8.5.
- (e) `delete this` on releasing thread: **RESOLVED BY STRUCTURE** [vixy: 2026-07-11] — see §8.2.5: lightweight render-chain finalization tasks carry the releases, so the last release lands on the render thread by construction; the checkable hand-off rule is `[inferred — pending convergence]`.
- (f) `TASKABLE_TASK_KEEP_REFERENCE` acquire/release asymmetry (found 2026-07-11, second pass): `execute()`'s empty-chain branch acquires but `scheduleExecution()`'s does not, while `endTask`'s CAS-success releases unconditionally → scheduled-mode chain start with both ifdefs on underflows the refcount → premature delete. **MOOT under the chosen granularity** [vixy: 2026-07-11]: single-chain synchronization, all Taskables application-lifetime, flags off. Remains **latent** — must be fixed before any per-body-chain split enables the flag (reopening trigger in §8.2.5).
**Defects in existing `AsyncLoaderMgr` (pre-dating, lower priority — the port supersedes them)**: `addLoad`/`addBuild` `push_front` without holding the list spinlock while workers iterate under it (list-head data race); `AsyncLoader::priority` is plain (non-atomic) but written by worker and main threads (`AsyncBuilder::priority` is atomic — the asymmetry looks unintended); `update()`'s lock-busy branch iterates the list without the lock while a worker may scan it.

The external world reaches the body system exclusively through `SSystemFactory` (callers: coreLink.cpp, core.cpp, executorModule). Per category, where each call routes when the new path is active (`drawModularSystem`). "dual" = already routed to both paths today.

| Category | Old-surface examples | New-path route |
|---|---|---|
| Selection/search | setSelected, searchByNamesI18, searchAround, listMatchingObjectsI18n | `ModularBody::findBody*` + `ModularBodySelector` + `ModularObject` (B7 surface); pointer draw via ObjectBase::drawPointer over ModularObject (D2) |

| Color | setBodyColor/getBodyColor, setDefaultBodyColor | **RUNTIME SETTERS DUAL (2026-07-22, §11.65, B29)**: per-body recolor (halo=body, label/orbit/trail=modules, self-select I4) + `"all"` broadcast + runtime DEFAULT (module statics) mirror to the new path; per-instance storage + broadcast override (§11.48(b)); getter old-authority pre-switchover (§11.46). Runtime colour PERSISTENCE across `body action reload` = B16 §11.55(i)'s suspended body-scoped-override decision, NOT closed here (old has no reload ⇒ no observable to reproduce; new rebuilds-from-file resets, measured) |
| Flags | setFlagHints/Axis/Trails/Orbits/Clouds, setPlanetHidden, toggleHideSatellites | module static `show` flags (HintModule etc.) + `ModularBody::hide/show`; per-name orbit flag = per-body module toggle |
| Textures | switchPlanetTexMap, createTexSkin, planetTesselation | **ALL DUAL (2026-07-19, §11.46)**: skin pair = `BodyModule::createTexSkin/switchTexSkin` broadcast (MESH modules consume, old tex_current parity) + factory mirrors; tesselation was ALREADY dual by shared `BodyTesselation` object (row 2 §11.26 — the T7 audit row claiming OLD-ONLY was wrong, correction at §11.45) |
| Body add/remove | addBody, preloadBody, removeBody, removeSupplementalBodies | `ModularSystem::loadBody` (dual for removeBody already); preload = `ModularBody::preload`. **New-path-only addition (2026-07-21, §11.55): `body action reload` → `SSystemFactory::reloadCurrentSystem` → `ModularSystem::reloadSystem`** — rebuild the current system from its data file, observer state kept; no old-path counterpart |

## 10. Renderer pipeline-family API — requirements (2026-07-11) + design (§10.3)

D2's blocker. §10.1/10.2 are observed need, not invented design; the design itself now exists (§10.3 + `PipelineFamily.hpp` + the registry block in `Renderer.hpp`, 2026-07-11) — headers written, implementation deliberately absent, pending Vixy convergence. B3's contract already fixes the frame: modules DESCRIBE (traits + descriptor contract), the Renderer EXECUTES (owns every drawState).

### 10.1 What it must manage
- **Pipeline families** replacing `SHADER_USE`/`selectShader` [observed: bodyShader.hpp:41-60]: mesh-layered (the hard one: night/clouds/specular/bump/tesselation feature COMBINATIONS — the old encoded them as enum entries + `pipelineOffset` variants [observed: body_bigbody.hpp:92]), OJM/model (± shadowed), ring (+ instanced-asteroid + depth-trace variants), lines (orbit/trail/axis/grid — depth-tested and depth-free variants), screen-space 2D (hint circle, pointer), big-halo/star, translucent shell (AtmExt), tail.
- **Per-pass variants**: a family must provide its variant per pass kind it participates in — COLOR, NO-DEPTH, SELF-SHADOW, SHADOW-STENCIL, TRACE [BodyModule.hpp hooks] — keyed at least by (family, pass, feature-variant). Old path had explicit SHADOW/DEPTH_TRACE drawStates [observed: bodyShader.hpp].
- **Render-pass compatibility**: pipelines are bound to FrameMgr passes (`PASS_MULTISAMPLE_DEPTH` etc. [observed: Renderer.cpp beginDraw; body.cpp:1036-1068]); self-shadow targets variable-size attachments (8192 main / 2048 secondary [ModularBody.hpp constants]) → dynamic viewport or per-resolution builds.
- **Descriptor machinery**: set layouts per family; set allocation for modules (BasicMesh owns an EntityCore `Set` [observed: BasicMesh.hpp]); big-texture rebind generations (`bigTexRecap::binding` [observed: s_texture.hpp:97-108], old `bigSet` lazy rebuild [observed: body_bigbody.cpp:445-478]); **descriptor POOL sizing per family needs** — live evidence this is currently broken: one `vkAllocateDescriptorSets` validation error per run, pool created without `VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_SAMPLED_IMAGE` (§11.2).
- **Batching as a Renderer service**, dissolving the global batchers (`Halo::global` beginDraw/nextDraw/endDraw [observed: halo.hpp:66-70], `Tail::global` [observed: tail.hpp:43-46]): begin/submit/flush per family at pass boundaries; `BMT_REPLICATED` is the declared hint.
- **Global config → specialization**: tesselation levels (`BodyTesselation`, shared static [observed: body_tesselation.hpp]) and dynamic-resolution (`BMT_DYNAMIC`) parameterize pipeline builds → config changes trigger REBUILDS (work-domain) with publish-swap, never in-frame stalls.
- **The two existing old-path borrows to absorb first** — **BOTH DISSOLVED (2026-07-12, S1; measurements §11.22)**: `BasicMesh` now draws through the MESH family (MeshFamilies.cpp; bodyShader include gone, globalVertProj/globalFrag re-homed to meshModules/bodyShaderInterface.hpp with bodyShader.hpp including back — old→new edge dying with the old path); `Renderer` halo drawing runs on the batching service (HALO service family, Halo::global untouched by the new path; texture via the `setTexHaloMap` seam mirror). ~~The hint DrawHelper seam entry remains~~ — **DISSOLVED (2026-07-12, §11.24)** with the HINT-family completion, as planned (that code was touched exactly once): DRAW_HINT_POS/s_hintPos/drawHintPos removed, hint circles ride the HINT batched service family.

### 10.2 Constraints it must satisfy
- **C1/effective-thread**: registry mutation (new pipeline published, variant swapped) = chain task; pipeline USE within the frame task is read-only. Creation is heavy (old path: static init + 4 dedicated shadow-pipeline build threads [observed: context.cpp:79-83]) → creation is WORK-DOMAIN (AsyncBuilder fits), publication is a publish task.
- **C3**: never build-on-first-use synchronously in the frame. Corollary — **base-variant-always-ready**: each family keeps one variant resident from init, mirroring D6's lowest-LoD-always-resident (something drawable always exists; a missing fancy variant degrades, never stalls). Same ladder philosophy, pipelines instead of textures.
- **D5 budget**: do NOT precompile the feature-combination cross-product (2 GiB floor); lazy variant builds via work domain + the EntityCore pipelineCache for fast rebuild [observed: "No changes in the pipelineCache" shutdown log].
- **Trait-driven routing**: the Renderer routes a module through exactly the passes its BMT_* traits declare (a trait not declared = a pass never received [BodyModule.hpp contract]); MINOR_BODY exemption applies at body level above module traits.
- **Frame structure**: per-frameIdx command buffers, 3 frames in flight [observed: Context, app.cpp:373-408]; teardown order deterministic (old `deleteShader` pattern).
- **Text is a delegation, not a family**: labels go through the Projector gravity-text path + shared s_font [observed: hints.cpp:72] — the API must expose access to that path (or the frame task's Projector), not reimplement text.

### 10.3 The design (2026-07-11, headers written — pending Vixy convergence)

Authoritative contract: `PipelineFamily.hpp` + the registry block in `Renderer.hpp` (headers are the medium; this section records decisions, evidence and opens — not the contract itself).

Evidence base: 3 file:line-backed sweeps (old-path pipeline inventory / EntityCore capabilities / new-path borrow surface). Scale being replaced: ~41 shared old-path graphics pipelines + 3 per Sun/Star instance + 3 per Ring instance + ≤255 shadow-blur ComputePipelines.

Decisions, each with the fact that forced it:
1. **Exactly four PassKinds = the four drawing types; NO-DEPTH is the reserved variant bit `VARIANT_NO_DEPTH`, not a pass.** All body-path color/trace/line/halo pipelines live in ONE subpass (PASS_BACKGROUND==PASS_MULTISAMPLE_DEPTH==0 [observed: context.hpp:43-49]); no-depth is pipeline state (old `pipelineNoDepth = pipeline+2` [observed: bodyShader.cpp:128]); ringed's legitimate no-depth non-support [observed: body.cpp:1055-1059] maps onto bit-drop fallback. Real separate render passes exist only for shadows and already exist [observed: app.cpp:347-363, renderSelfShadow/renderShadow].
2. **Bind-and-record**: a module calls `bind(family, wanted)` (resolved against the Renderer's current pass kind — a COLOR pipeline structurally cannot bind while TRACE records) then records its own geometry. Retained draw-description submission rejected: per-draw marshalling on the hot path for zero safety gain, forbids module-owned record patterns (ObjL::bind/draw), contradicts G10 + the normative `operator VkCommandBuffer`. Reopen only if a pass appears whose recording the render chain cannot serialize. [open #1]
3. **Variant model**: uint16 feature bits; axes declare effect (SPEC_CONSTANT | SHADER_SWAP | STATE_OVERRIDE) + dropPriority; base variant of every declared pass built synchronously at registration (base-always-ready ← C3, mirrors D6 lowest-LoD-resident); non-base variants lazy in the work domain, published as a chain task (← C1; precedent: 4-thread shadow builds + atomic publish [observed: context.cpp:79-100]; pipelineCache concurrent use is legal); never the cross-product (← D5). EntityCore's 3-update deferred pipeline destroy [observed: Pipeline.hpp:70] covers publish-swap across frames in flight. SHADER_SWAP axes port today's distinct shader files unchanged; a future layered mesh shader collapses them into SPEC_CONSTANT axes with no API change.
4. **Layout-invariance hard rule**: a variant axis never changes the descriptor contract — (family, pass) → layout is constant; layout-changing features are separate families. Evidence: artificial vs artificialShadowed set-count divergence [observed: bodyShader.cpp:240-285]; myEarthShadowed omits the global UBO set that shaderShadowedTes includes [observed: bodyShader.cpp:359-370 vs 385-395] — normalized at port, not reproduced.
5. **Declarative descriptor contract → pool aggregation**: the same SetDesc data builds the PipelineLayout and sizes Renderer-owned pools — a pool is always sized from the layouts it serves; structural closure of the §11.1 error class (new-path scope; the live old-path instance needs the EntityCore fix, open #2).
6. **Batching as a Renderer service under the occlusion contract** [vixy: 2026-07-11]: batched screen-space content (halo, hint) occluded as-if drawn farthest→closest against bodies — flush at the per-body command-buffer boundaries, the mechanism already live [observed: Renderer.cpp:36-59]; halo↔hint mutual order inside a segment is free whenever it improves performance. Dissolves `Halo::global` (+ the Renderer friend-poke into its pData), Tail's ride-on-halo coupling [observed: halo.cpp:55,72], and the DrawHelper hint batch at the seam. **Scope note** [vixy: 2026-07-11]: "per-category order" is EnvironmentModule frame-sequencing (§3.8), NOT a batch-flush rule.
7. **Frame context on the Renderer** (Projector/Navigator set before beginDraw) — **INVALIDATED** [vixy: 2026-07-11, review]: Projector/Navigator are old-path projection machinery (system-center reference); the new path doesn't use them at all — projection rides the parent↔child matrix chain routed through the closest common parent between Camera and target (better precision by construction). Delegating labels to Projector would carry old-path state into new-path drawing — the exact borrow class this API dissolves. The gravity-text machinery must be partially rewritten against the new chain (duplicate code between paths is possible); the module-facing channel is redefined by the projection-path investigation (§11.14). Header carriage removed. [open #3 → investigation delivered a proposal: Renderer text service as a pure function of `screenPos` + viewport + font — printGravity180's frame-matrix dependency was apparent, not real (projection-paths.md C7); pending Vixy convergence]
8. **Compute families in the same registry** (kind=COMPUTE; shadow-blur bank = one family, radius = variant, EAGER_ASYNC_ALL policy reproducing today's behavior); dispatch-side ergonomics deferred to G7's shadow implementation. [open #4]
9. **Describe-once → descriptor paradigm** [vixy: 2026-07-11, header review — supersedes the first C-shaped draft]: descriptions are one-time cold-path costs, so they use owning types (std::string/std::vector — lifetime correctness by construction, no externally-asserted `const char*`/pointer-array clauses); allocation returns a descriptor (integer index wrapped in `RegistryHandle<Tag>`: copies share via registry refcount, destruction releases implicitly); hot paths carry only the index; all enums are `enum class`, declared before use. Structural payoff: the SetRole enum (FAMILY_OWNED/GLOBAL_UBO/EXTERNAL) **dissolved** — all three were ownership cases of one mechanism, "a `SetContract` allocated once, referenced by handle" (global UBO = a pre-allocated contract via `globalUboContract()`; traceLayout sharing = the same handle held by two families; a desc holding handles keeps its references alive by construction). Root cause of the first draft's shape, traced: hot-path constraints (zero-alloc, static tables) misapplied to a cold path + matching existing style weighed over long-run optimality — the criterion "optimal in the long run (decades), code debt prevention is critical, not nice-to-have" [vixy: 2026-07-11] now explicit.

Coverage check (every §10.1 family walked against the inventory; the walk itself forced two contract additions — `FixedState::stripBreaks` [Tail's primitive-restart strips, observed: tail.cpp] and `SpecConstant` device/config-derived values [float64 id 7 across families, sun big-halo viewport height, artificialShadowed shadow resolution — the "global config → specialization" input, rebuilt-not-stalled on change]; after which every family is expressible without struct change): mesh-layered (SHADER_SWAP now → spec-const later) · OJM + OJM_SHADOWED (rule 4) · RING color+trace, RING_ASTEROID instanced+batched · orbit/trail/axis/grid as separate families where push-constant contracts differ · HINT (batched) / POINTER · SUN / SUN_HALO / STAR_VIEWER / CORONA · ATM_EXT (SRC_ALPHA + MAX blend-op expressible in FixedState) · TAIL (instanced batch, shared geometry via VertexArray instance-rate) · trace/self-shadow/shadow-shape = Renderer-owned service families (traceLayout sharing = one SetContract held by both families). Sun/pointer prebuilt static command buffers dissolve into frame-task recording at port time (C1 requires it anyway).

**Open convergence points** — (1)–(5) **RESOLVED [vixy: 2026-07-12, plan approval — the approved plan carried these as explicit recommendations; approval = acceptance; if any was not intended as such, flag and it reopens]**: (1) bind-and-record confirmed as the module contract. (2) SetMgr SAMPLED_IMAGE pool-table fix in EntityCore — authorized, applied uncommitted in the submodule (precedent: Taskable/ASmooth edits). (3) label/text channel: Renderer text service, pure function of `screenPos` + viewport + font (projection-paths.md C7) — accepted. (4) compute dispatch deferred to G7 — accepted. (5) variant budget uint16, bit 15 reserved — sufficient. (6) depth-slice margin policy — **RESOLVED** [vixy: 2026-07-11]: boundingRadius is DEFINED as the smallest sphere enclosing the whole traced body — inclusive by definition, which is exactly why one value serves both the visibility cone test and depth bounding; no margin factor (the old 1.1 compensated a non-inclusive radius). Documented at BodyModule.hpp member + Renderer.hpp clearDepth. Consequence: a module whose drawn extent exceeds its mesh radius (terrain, shells, rings) must RETURN that larger radius from update() — the contract, not a renderer guard, carries the safety.

182. **A '#' OUTSIDE QUOTES IS A COMMENT — RULED BEHAVIOUR, MODELLED BY SCEDIT FIRST, THEN LANDED IN `parseCommand` (2026-08-31, Claude Fable 5; code `3d9179d2`; compiled on GCC 11, NOT run — no display).** Rulings [vixy]: 2026-08-30 "the ENGINE will treat mid-line `#` as a real comment" (the legacy defect only "passed" because unrecognized keys are inert; precondition: quoting-aware); 2026-08-31, on scedit's morning seed for the HEAD defect: *"# loop on is a comment, not to be parsed as syntax"* and the ORDER *"make scedit track what the HEAD would be after the behavior get corrected, then we correct spacecrafter to be in face"* — scedit's C1 amended accordingly (the oracle's copy of parseCommand is the TARGET; the engine receives the identical block; verbatim again on landing — this entry). Rule, twelve lines at the top of `parseCommand` (app_command_interface.cpp:124-): a `#` outside a `"…"` run ends the command; quotes counted by a plain toggle from byte 0; the cut runs BEFORE the leading-blank strip and the ` " ` normalisation, so an INDENTED `#` is a whole-line comment; `commandline` (what the recorder writes, :1167) is the line before the cut, so recordings keep comments. Placement decision [fable, veto open]: parseCommand — the one choke point every channel passes (file, addScriptFirst splice, TCP, HTTP, pipe, joypad, the nested executeCommand calls of `clear`/`media`) — over script-layer-only, whose two classifier sites already diverge on indentation; observable difference only on live channels with an unquoted `#`, and none exists: no ini command string carries `#`, HTTP's `?command=` never delivers a raw `#`. Shape decision [fable, veto open]: "outside quotes, `#` starts a comment" (python-style, simplest at the zero-knowledge bar) over shell-style word-start — measured to agree on the whole corpus (408 shipped + witness + harness: `#` glued outside quotes 0, `#` inside quotes 0, word-start `#` 106 = 98 indented whole-line comments + `doc/superscript.sts:37-46`). Effects: the 8 witness lines are correct as written (SS-20 resolved in-tree); **98 indented comments in the shipped scripts stop executing as unknown commands** (one log line per run each, until now); the future `#!` machine annotation (FEATURE_REQUESTS 2026-08-30) is a comment by this rule — its ordering clause (1) is satisfied; scedit seeds `inline-comment`/`indented-comment` retired, oracle 119 337 comparisons / 0 mismatches with `#` in the alphabet, 408-script findings 1759 → 1661 (diff minus the indented ones EMPTY). OWED: live confirmation on a running engine (a script with trailing comments, a quoted `#`, an indented `#`; a TCP line with `#`); the `#!` writer itself; mod/div/mul aliases (FEATURE_REQUESTS carries the recorder-spelling trap). **[2026-08-31 → §11.183: live confirmation PAID (F61 16/16, RED control 8/16 on `a3437670`); aliases LANDED (`7fd5ea75`, F62 11/11); the "recorder-spelling trap" CORRECTED — the map it named has no consumer; the `#!` writer stays owed.]** Full record: scedit INTENT journal 2026-08-31b; derivation-diff §1 (new row), §5.10 (superseded), §7.5.

185. **THE ENGINE TELLS A TCP CLIENT NOTHING ABOUT A SCRIPT IT PLAYS — AND F27'S ADDRESSED REPLY IS CONFIRMED LIVE BY AN INDEPENDENT CLIENT (2026-08-31, Claude Opus 5 executor, task F67, dispatched by Claude Fable 5; NO ENGINE CODE — recorded with its workaround and routed, never fixed; instrument `harness/f67_tcp_live.py` 28/28 over two fresh launches, artifacts `harness/artifacts/f67/`).** A client on 7805, subscribed with `$LOGON`, played a script carrying one block fault; the engine ran it, wrote its `#!` diagnosis into the file and reached its natural end, and **the connection received ZERO bytes for the whole play after the subscription's own confirmation** `[measured: leg D]` — no start, no end, no diagnostic. Not a property of that script: **only two things ever reach a client**, the answer to `get status …`/`search name …` `[observed: app_command_interface.cpp:1284-1301,:1415 — the only callers of `setOutput` in the tree]` and the inline `$NOTICE`/`$LOGON`/`$LOGOFF` replies `[observed: io.cpp:640-663]`; everything else, including *"Unable to execute script : <path>"* `[:2889]`, goes to `debug_message` and thence to §5.117's log. Positive control in the same run: a `get status position` on that same connection IS answered `[leg B]` — the channel works, nothing is addressed to it about a script. Consequence: from the wire alone a client cannot tell a command that ran from one that was refused, a script still playing from one that ended, or a normal end from a file that could not be opened. The census's PLACE/SOLVER keys give **twelve** such bodies, not fourteen (`Hiiaka`/`Namaka` are e = 0 and hold no seed). **THE NARROW MUTATION** (the JD-0 evaluation KEPT, only the seed it leaves reset) moves **EXACTLY Eris and Sedna** of the 120 — the committed prediction by name — Eris onto the POST binary's landed float32 value with sep_p0 1.1987248926314011° → **1.0629396175241108e-05° at ONE step per call**, Sedna **75 AU OFF** it (sep_p0 55.018°) because `IterativeEll` starts at (0, 1, 0) and its first step is `H = M/(1−e)` = 44 rad at e = 0.8588: for the comet family the JD-0 call BURNS that bad step, for Eris's branch it CREATES the staleness. **So the 1.198725° was a seed-ORIGIN defect, not a step-count one.** The DISPATCHED mutation shape (skip the evaluation) moved **49** records and is kept REFUTED with its cause: `isSystemCentered()` answers by POSITION `[ModularBody.hpp:1788-1800]` and both orbit loaders ask it at LOAD TIME, so the constructor's evaluation has a SECOND consumer and “skip it” is not a fix shape. **(j2) IN THE ENGINE**, four launches, every comparison dump-to-dump INSIDE one launch (within-launch control **0 of 120** four times; other-date control 90 of 120): a parked body is ERASED from `sortedSystemBodies` and never sampled; **`flag planets_orbits on` moves NOTHING while changing 91774 pixels** (every walked iterating record is a SATELLITE, `[OrbitModule.cpp:91]` + `[ModularBody.hpp:1128-1130]`); **P5 HELD — 0 of 40 walked-iterative records move** under `flag satellites_orbits on`, with the 1-frame blind spot named in advance; but that flag moves **17 `*_special` records PERSISTENTLY** (Mimas 1.8726e-07 AU = 28 km) through `CalcInterpolatedElements`' STATIC three-epoch cache `[tass17.c:3146-3151]`, which the moons ride because they have no osculating function — and a third mutation attributes **16 of the 17 to the OLD path's own plot and EXACTLY ONE to the new path's sampler: Europa, 3.475e-08 AU**. ### 13.D External inputs (companion files, single authority — 2026-07-20)

**[2026-07-22 repo split: this file and every companion file below now live together in the `claude/` nested repository (branch `CC-harness`, same host) — "repo root" in the paragraph below reads as pre-split history; layout + conventions in `README.md`. Companion-file refs to `src/experimentalModule/INTENT.md` were corrected to `INTENT.md` (same folder) the same day. A fourth companion, `DECISIONS_PENDING.md` (2026-07-21-wave residuals view, compiled 2026-07-22), follows the same authority rule: it owns no decision, this ledger wins on divergence.]**

Three files at repo root, outside this tree, so they're reachable without going through `experimentalModule`: **`USER_QUESTIONS.md`** — the rows that are genuinely user-observable behavior (not internal-architecture questions) translated to plain language, each tagged back to its `Axx`/`Bxx` ref for exact re-matching; answers resolve the corresponding row here, not a copy of it. **Coverage as of 2026-07-20 (expanded pass, addressed to a heavy early-release tester — planetarium/sky expertise assumed, implementation knowledge NOT assumed)**: 26 of the 29 §13.A rows — A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A7, A8, A9, A10, A11, A12, A13, A14, A15, A17, A18, A19, A20, A23, A24, A25, A26, A27, A28, A29 — plus **B4**; A23's question narrowed to a completeness check the same day (row resolved [vixy 2026-07-20], but "do your scripts use the two-body patch, and does a per-body boolean reproduce them?" is answerable only by a script author and validates B10's scope) (CameraAnchors: which anchor kinds are actually used decides the port's design, and only a user can answer it). Deliberately excluded, and the exclusion is stated *inside* the companion file so the tester can challenge it: A6, A16, A21, A22 (no user-visible surface) and the coordinate/threading B-rows. Two factual corrections landed in the same pass — the first draft's A12 question described the copy-paste cluster as *orbital* data causing *positional* error (it is `rot_obliquity`/`rot_equator_ascending_node` axial-orientation data causing up-to-155° *orientation* error, 28 bodies, Iapetus the one observable case), and its A5 question described `apparent_magnitude`/`slope` as brightness parameters (they are H/G driving coma diameter + tail length via the comet-tail formula, and no shipped body sets them — so the decisive sub-question is whether the tester's *scripts* set them). Both were derived-doc drift of exactly the §5.2 class: a companion file is a cached conclusion and needs re-verification against source, not recall. **`FEATURE_REQUESTS.md`** — the landing place for requests originating outside this tracker; created empty (no backfill — nothing invented to fill it), log format self-documented in the file. Triage direction is one-way and explicit: a logged request that turns into real work gets a row in §13 (A or B) with a pointer back to its `FEATURE_REQUESTS.md` entry; the entry's `Status` is then updated to point here — it does not get silently duplicated into a second untracked TODO. **Round 1 answered 2026-07-21 (tester, relayed by Vixy) and propagated the same day — full record §11.48**: 13 rows closed (§13.C list), 11 narrowed in place, 1 new row (A30), 13 implementation rows opened (B11–B23), 2 entries logged in `FEATURE_REQUESTS.md`. Round-2 questions ~~live at the bottom of `USER_QUESTIONS.md`~~ **moved to the dedicated `USER_QUESTIONS_ROUND2.md` (2026-07-21, Vixy's direction)** — live re-asks R1, R3–R11 (R8/R10 reframed per §11.51's resolutions: R8 = future-preference input under the parity meta-rule, R10 = completeness check on B27's code-extracted list; R11 stakes-dropped, both channels build regardless per B17), plus a no-longer-questions section: R2 (resolved §11.49(a), outcome stated with an explicit veto window — the tester's original answer was ambiguous, so stating the adopted behavior back is the cheap verification) and R12 (withdrawn, informational, updated with §11.52(c)'s naming). **Round 2 answered 2026-07-22 (tester, relayed by Vixy) and propagated — full record §11.70**: A28/A17/A18/A4/A27 resolved; B4's design-deciding half answered; B10 confirmed (patch purpose = fly-into/transparent bodies) with one derivation OVERTURNED by R4 (stop-and-hold at the lowest altitude, not the inward asymptote); B17/B20/B27/B29/B31 informed; R2 confirms A9. Numbering stable, `(ref:)` keys unchanged; the old round-2 section in `USER_QUESTIONS.md` is now a pointer (single authority, no fork). The split by **who can answer** (tester-only = what shows/scripts actually do; Vixy = design authority) was round 2's correction of a round-1 defect — some round-1 questions went to the party who could not answer them. Round 1's own two failures are carried in §11.48(d) and constrain round 2: **name the observable, never the engine's internal vocabulary** (the `ring_shadow` failure — a document that declares "implementation knowledge not assumed" and then assumes it), and **give options labels distinct from case labels** (the A9 failure — an answer's ambiguity is the question's defect). The tester also asked two questions back; those are answered at the top of round 2 — a companion file that only asks is a one-way channel, which is a self-imposed blind spot on the one party holding the shipped-show evidence. Neither file is authoritative over anything in §13.A–13.C; on disagreement (a question answered here but not reflected in USER_QUESTIONS.md's traceability note, or vice versa) this ledger wins per I2, and the divergence itself is a staleness bug to fix, not a fork to maintain.
